title.narrative: Promoting rural women’s Participation in Good and Inclusive Governance –Phase II

description.narrative:
Over the last couple of years, Sierra Leone has started demonstrating the political will to implement its commitment to gender equality and the promotion of women’s and girls’ rights through the passage of a number of legislations including: The Three Gender Acts 2007, The Sexual Offences Act 2012, The Child Rights Act 2007 and the development of a number of national programmes on the protection and advancement of women and girls at all levels of society.
Despite formal commitment and effort at the central and local level to enhance the welfare and participation of women, the women’s participation in Governance is still low especially in Kenema district where this project is located. Moreover, the inequalities and discrimination still persist especially in the rural communities in the Kenema district. As a result, the women and girls continue to be the most vulnerable and disadvantaged in present day Sierra Leone. They remain under-represented in decision-making but over-represented among the poor.
While they represent an approximate 51.3% of the population in Sierra Leone, they still remain absent or in some cases excluded from governance and decision making processes. The UNDP report on women in Sierra Leone confirms that they are disproportionately disadvantaged by the measures of human poverty. A lack of formal education particularly the illiteracy of roughly four in every five women-frequently brings with it diminished self-confidence in formal communication and negotiation (UNDP Annual Report 2011). This is a major barrier to women’s engagement and involvement in governance and decision making processes and is also being used to further perpetuate their disadvantaged situation. Low levels of schooling are compounded by inadequate opportunity for self-empowerment resulting in a heavy dependence on their male folks. General trends in the Sierra Leonean political and governance scene indicate that women continue to significantly lag behind in representation at all levels. Therefore to address these situations, the project intends to educate communities so women are able to participate, transform systems to improve women’s right; and move beyond the traditional economic empowerment of women. Specifically the project will build the capacities of local women to participate in local governance systems: chiefdom and district levels through life skills, adult education and engage them in savings and small business.
